# Cross-Validation
Prepare the data:
```{r}
library(MASS)
library(tidyverse)
data(Boston)
boston <- Boston %>% dplyr::select(crim, rm, zn, chas, ptratio, medv)
```

## The validation set approach
```{r class.source="bg-danger"}
n <- nrow(boston)
set.seed(1)
tr_ind <- sample(n, round(n/2))
boston_tr <- boston[tr_ind, ]
boston_val <- boston[-tr_ind, ] #validation set

mod_formula_seq <- c("medv ~ rm",
                     "medv ~ rm + ptratio",
                     "medv ~ rm + ptratio + zn",
                     "medv ~ rm + ptratio + zn + crim")
cv_mse_seq <- numeric(4)
names(cv_mse_seq) <- mod_formula_seq
for (i in 1:4) {
  form <- as.formula(mod_formula_seq[i])
  fit <- lm(form, data = boston_tr)
  pred <- predict(fit, newdata = boston_val)
  cv_mse_seq[i] <- mean((pred - boston_val$medv)^2)
}
cv_mse_seq
```


## Leave-One-Out Cross-Validation (LOOCV)

```{r class.source="bg-danger"}
mod_formula_seq <- c("medv ~ rm",
                     "medv ~ rm + ptratio",
                     "medv ~ rm + ptratio + zn",
                     "medv ~ rm + ptratio + zn + crim")
cv_mse_seq <- numeric(4)
names(cv_mse_seq) <- mod_formula_seq
for (i in 1:4) {
  form <- as.formula(mod_formula_seq[i])
  pred <- numeric(n)
  for (j in 1:nrow(boston)) {
    fit <- lm(form, data = boston[-j, ])
    pred[j] <- predict(fit, newdata = boston[j, ])
  }
  cv_mse_seq[i] <- mean((pred - boston$medv)^2)
}
cv_mse_seq
```

```{r}
library(boot)
mod_formula_seq <- c("medv ~ rm",
                     "medv ~ rm + ptratio",
                     "medv ~ rm + ptratio + zn",
                     "medv ~ rm + ptratio + zn + crim")
cv_mse_seq <- numeric(4)
names(cv_mse_seq) <- mod_formula_seq
for (i in 1:4) {
  form <- as.formula(mod_formula_seq[i])
  fit <- glm(form, data = boston)
  cv_mse_seq[i] <- cv.glm(boston, fit)$delta[1]
}
cv_mse_seq
```


## $k$-fold CV for model selection

- Suppose in the `Default` dataset, we are deciding between three models 
- model 1: use `rm` to predict `medv`
- model 2: use `rm` and `ptratio` to predict `medv`
- model 3: use `rm`, `ptratio`, and `zn` to predict `medv`
- To choose between these three models using 5-fold CV, we calculate $CV_{(5)}$ for models 1, 2, 3 and choose the model with the smallest $CV_{(5)}$. 
- The same idea extends to the case where we need to choose among many models.  


    ```{r class.source="bg-danger"}
    ##K-Fold CV
    K <- 5
    n <- nrow(boston)
    set.seed(1)
    fold_ind <- sample(rep_len(1:K, n)) # randomly split dataset into K folds
    mod_formula_seq <- c("medv ~ rm",
                         "medv ~ rm + ptratio",
                         "medv ~ rm + ptratio + zn",
                         "medv ~ rm + ptratio + zn + crim")
    cv_mse_seq <- numeric(4)
    names(cv_mse_seq) <- mod_formula_seq
    for (i in 1:4) {
      form <- as.formula(mod_formula_seq[i])
      pred <- numeric(n)
      for (j in 1:K) {
        fit <- lm(form, data = boston[fold_ind != j, ])
        pred[fold_ind == j] <- predict(fit, newdata = boston[fold_ind == j, ])
      }
      cv_mse_seq[i] <- mean((pred - boston$medv)^2)
    }
    cv_mse_seq
    ```


    ```{r}
    library(boot)
    mod_formula_seq <- c("medv ~ rm",
                         "medv ~ rm + ptratio",
                         "medv ~ rm + ptratio + zn",
                         "medv ~ rm + ptratio + zn + crim")
    cv_mse_seq <- numeric(4)
    names(cv_mse_seq) <- mod_formula_seq
    for (i in 1:4) {
      form <- as.formula(mod_formula_seq[i])
      fit <- glm(form, data = boston)
      set.seed(1)
      cv_mse_seq[i] <- cv.glm(boston, fit, K = 5)$delta[1]
    }
    cv_mse_seq
    ```

## Use $k$-fold CV for classification 

- The basic idea of CV for classification is the same as that for regression, except the way to calculate $CV_{(k)}$
    + For example, the LOOCV error rate is 
$$
CV_{(n)} = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n Err_i\,,
$$
    + where $Err_i = I_{y_i \neq {\hat y}_i}$

    ```{r class.source="bg-danger"}
    library(tidyverse)
    library(ISLR)
    K <- 5
    n <- nrow(Default)
    set.seed(1)
    fold_ind <- sample(rep_len(1:K, n))
    mod_formula_seq <- c("default ~ balance",
                         "default ~ balance + income")
    cv_error_seq <- numeric(2)
    names(cv_error_seq) <- mod_formula_seq
    for (i in 1:2) {
      form <- as.formula(mod_formula_seq[i])
      pred <- factor(levels = levels(Default$default)) # initialize a (categorical) factor for y_hat
      for (j in 1:K) {
        fit <- glm(form, data = Default[fold_ind != j, ],
                   family = "binomial")
        pred_prob <- predict(fit, newdata = Default[fold_ind == j, ],
                             type = "response")
        pred_label <- ifelse(pred_prob > 0.5, "Yes", "No")
        pred[fold_ind == j] <- pred_label
      }
      cv_error_seq[i] <- mean(pred != Default$default)
    }
    cv_error_seq
    ```


## Choosing the $K$ in KNN

```{r class.source="bg-danger"}
library(caret)
library(ISLR)
K <- 5 # number of folds
n <- nrow(Default)
set.seed(1)
fold_ind <- sample(rep_len(1:K, n))
K_seq <- seq(from = 1, to = 300, by = 30) # number of neighbors for KNN
cv_error_seq <- numeric(length(K_seq))
for (i in seq_along(K_seq)) {
  K_cur <- K_seq[i]
  pred_knn <- factor(levels = levels(Default$default))
  for (j in 1:K) {
    fit_knn <- knn3(default ~ balance,
                    data = Default[fold_ind != j, ], k = K_cur)
    pred_knn[fold_ind == j] <-
      predict(fit_knn, newdata = Default[fold_ind == j, ], type = "class")
    }
  cv_error_seq[i] <- mean(pred_knn != Default$default)
  }
```

```{r class.source="bg-danger"}
knn_re <- data.frame(K = K_seq, CV_error = cv_error_seq)
ggplot(knn_re, mapping = aes(x = K, y = CV_error)) +
  geom_point(size = 1) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1)
```
